<module id="asyn_fifo">
    <description>Implement an asynchronous FIFO, FIFO bit width and depth can be configured(parameter DEPTH = 16, parameter WIDTH = 8). The asynchronous FIFO structure is divided into several parts. The first part is dual-port RAM, which is used for data storage. Instantiate dual-port RAM as a submodule, The RAM ports are input wclk, input wenc, input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] waddr, input [WIDTH-1:0] wdata, input rclk, input renc, input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] raddr, output reg [WIDTH-1:0] rdata. The second part is the data write controller. The third part is the data read controller. The fourth part is the read pointer synchronizer. The read pointer is collected using the two-stage trigger of the write clock and output to the data write controller. The fifth part is the write pointer synchronizer, which uses the two-stage trigger of the read clock to collect the write pointer and output it to the data read controller.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="wclk">Write clock signal used for synchronous write operations.</input>
        <input id="rclk">Read clock signal used for synchronous read operations.</input>
        <input id="wrstn">Write reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="rrstn">Read reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="winc">Write increment signal. Used to trigger write operations.</input>
        <input id="rinc">Read increment signal. Used to trigger read operations.</input>
        <input id="wdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Write data input. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data to be written into the FIFO.</input>
        <output id="wfull">Write full signal. Indicates if the FIFO is full and cannot accept further write operations.</output>
        <output id="rempty">Read empty signal. Indicates if the FIFO is empty and cannot provide any data for read operations.</output>
        <output id="rdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Read data output. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data read from the FIFO.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH">8. Internal parameter.</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH">16. Internal parameter.</parameter>
        <parameter id="ADDR_WIDTH">4. Internal parameter.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential id="raddr_bin">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] raddr_bin; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. raddr_bin size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If rrstn is deactive, raddr_bin is all zero. Otherwise, raddr_bin is incremented by 1 if rempty is deactive and rinc is active.</sequential>
        <combinational id="raddr_gray">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] raddr_gray; combinational logic. raddr_gray is XOR operation between raddr_bin and shift-left-1 operation of raddr_bin.</combinational>
        <sequential id="rptr">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. rptr size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, rptr is all zero. Otherwise, rptr is set to raddr_gray.</sequential>
        <sequential id="rptr_buff">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr_buff; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. rptr_buff size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, rptr_buff is all zero. Otherwise, rptr_buff is set to rptr.</sequential>
        <sequential id="rptr_syn">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr_syn; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. rptr_syn size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, rptr_syn is all zero. Otherwise, rptr_syn is set to rptr_buff.</sequential>
        <combinational id="ren">reg ren; combinational logic. Internal read enable logic. ren is active if rinc is active and rempty is deactive.</combinational>
        <sequential id="waddr_bin">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] waddr_bin; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. waddr_bin size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, waddr_bin is all zero. Otherwise, waddr_bin is incremented by 1 if wfull is deactive and winc is active.</sequential>
        <combinational id="waddr_gray">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] waddr_gray; combinational logic. waddr_gray is XOR operation between waddr_bin and shift-left-1 operation of waddr_bin.</combinational>
        <sequential id="wptr">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. wptr size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, wptr is all zero. Otherwise, wptr is set to waddr_gray.</sequential>
        <combinational id="wfull">reg wfull; combinational logic. The wfull output is set to 1 when the wptr is equal to the bitwise negation of the 2 most significant bits of the rptr_syn concatenated with the remaining bits of the rptr_syn.</combinational>
        <sequential id="wptr_buff">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr_buff; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. wptr_buff size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If rrstn is deactive, wptr_buff is all zero. Otherwise, wptr_buff is set to wptr.</sequential>
        <sequential id="wptr_syn">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr_syn; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. wptr_syn size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If rrstn is deactive, wptr_syn is all zero. Otherwise, wptr_syn is set to wptr_buff.</sequential>
        <combinational id="wen">reg wen; combinational logic. Internal write enable logic. wen is active if winc is active and wfull is deactive.</combinational>
        <combinational id="rempty">reg rempty; combinational logic. rempty is active if rptr is equaled to wptr_syn.</combinational>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        The module implements an asynchronous FIFO using a dual-port RAM module and additional logic for managing read and write pointers.
        Dual-port RAM:
        The module instantiates a dual-port RAM module named "dual_port_RAM" with configurable depth and width.  
        The RAM module has separate clock inputs for write (wclk) and read (rclk) operations.
        The RAM module has separate address inputs for write (waddr) and read (raddr) operations.
        The RAM module has a write enable input (wenc) and a write data input (wdata).
        The RAM module has a read enable input (renc) and a read data output (rdata).
        The RAM module stores data in a two-dimensional array, RAM_MEM, with a size of DEPTH by WIDTH.
        The following logics from the top module asyn_fifo are used to instantiates the dual_port_RAM: wclk, wen, waddr, wdata, rclk, ren, raddr, rdata:
        - wclk to wclk of asyn_fifo.
        - wen to wen of asyn_fifo.
        - waddr to waddr of asyn_fifo.
        - wdata to wdata of asyn_fifo.
        - rclk to rclk of asyn_fifo.
        - ren to ren of asyn_fifo.
        - raddr to raddr of asyn_fifo.
        - rdata to rdata of asyn_fifo.
        Write and Read Pointers:
        The module includes logic to manage write and read pointers for asynchronous operation.
        The write and read pointers are represented by binary registers, waddr_bin and raddr_bin, respectively.
        The waddr_bin and raddr_bin pointers are incremented based on the write and read increment signals (winc and rinc), respectively.
        The write pointer waddr_bin is incremented on the positive edge of the write clock (posedge wclk) and reset to 0 on write reset (~wrstn).
        The read pointer raddr_bin is incremented on the positive edge of the read clock (posedge rclk) and reset to 0 on read reset (~rrstn).
        Gray Code Conversion:
        The write and read pointers are converted to Gray code using XOR operations with right-shifted values.
        The converted write and read pointers are stored in registers wptr and rptr, respectively.
        The Gray code conversion reduces glitches and ensures proper synchronization of the write and read pointers.
